[[2:5|They shall quickly get upon the walls thereof|Velociter ascendent muros ejus]], that is, the Assyrians, seeking the safety of flight, shall go within the walls of their cities, above all of Ninive; [[2:5|and a covering shall be prepared|et præparabitur umbraculum]]. For both the Chaldeans besieging and the Assyrians besieged made themselves huts because of the heat of the sun, in which they escaped its burning. Some understand by the *covering* the tents of the Chaldeans, spread out round about Ninive.

paras.t: Portæ fluviorum apertæ sunt, id est portæ Ninivæ, ante quas aquarum currunt fluenta, et quæ multitudinem civium continebant tam copiosam, quod cives per flumina designantur. Hæ portæ a Chaldæis apertæ sunt atque destructæ. Et templum ad solum dirutum est, id est, fanum Nesroch quem coluit Sennacherib, in terram projectum est.
paras.en: [[2:6|The gates of the rivers are opened|Portæ fluviorum apertæ sunt]], that is, the gates of Ninive, before which streams of water flow, and which held so great a multitude of citizens that the citizens are signified by the rivers. These gates were opened and destroyed by the Chaldeans. [[2:6|And the temple is thrown down to the ground|Et templum ad solum dirutum]], that is, the shrine of Nesroch, whom Sennacherib worshipped[[4 Kings 19:37||]], was cast to the earth.

paras.t: Et miles captivus abductus est, id est, milites Assyriorum a Chaldæis partim translati sunt; et ancillæ ejus minabantur, id est, famulæ militum ab adversariis captæ sunt, et coram eis in Chaldæam translatæ pro parte, gementes ut columbæ, id est, intra se suspirantes propter instantia mala, murmurantes in cordibus suis, quia propter adversa ad impatientiam motæ sunt : tamen propter adversariorum fortitudinem et timorem, non audebant clamare et signa mœstitiæ foris ostendere, quemadmodum nec Chaldæi, quando a Medis vastabantur ac Persis, ut patet in Isaia. Quidam per ancillas intelligunt urbes Assyriorum subditas Ninive, sicut in libro Josue minores civitates seu villæ, dicuntur principalium urbium filiæ.
paras.en: [[2:7|And the soldier is led away captive|Et miles captivus abductus est]], that is, the soldiers of the Assyrians were in part carried away by the Chaldeans; [[2:7|and her bondwomen were led away|et ancillæ ejus minabantur]], that is, the soldiers' maidservants were taken by the enemy, and some of them carried off before them into Chaldea, [[2:7|mourning as doves|gementes ut columbæ]], that is, sighing within themselves because of the evils pressing upon them, [[2:7|murmuring in their hearts|murmurantes in cordibus suis]], because their adversities moved them to impatience; yet for the strength of their adversaries, and for fear, they did not dare to cry out and show signs of grief outwardly: just as neither did the Chaldeans when they were laid waste by the Medes and Persians, as is plain in Isaias[[Is 21:2||]]. Some understand by the *bondwomen* the cities of the Assyrians subject to Ninive, as in the book of Josue[[Jos 15:1||]] [the margin gives Josue xv–xix passim, the lists of the towns of the tribes] the lesser cities or villages are called the daughters of the principal cities[[1 Par 7:28||]][[1 Par 7:29||]][[1 Par 8:12||]].

paras.t: Et Ninive, quasi piscina aquarum aquæ ejus, id est Ninive, utpote multitudo populi ejus : aquæ enim multæ, populi multi, secundum Joannem in Apocalypsi. Vel, aquæ de quarum munitione Ninivitæ præsumpserunt, similes sunt aquæ piscinæ, non aquæ maris, id est inutiles ad resistendum Chaldæis. Ideo subditur : Ipsi vero fugerunt, id est, Ninivitæ et Assyrii a facie Chaldæorum fugerunt. Quibus fugientibus, alii constantiores clamant : State, state, id est, ne fugiatis, sed pugnetis; et non est qui revertatur, id est, nullus eorum redire audebat. Idcirco Chaldæis nunc dicitur :
paras.en: [[2:8|And as for Ninive, her waters are like a great pool|Et Ninive, quasi piscina aquarum aquæ ejus]]: *her waters*, that is, Ninive's, meaning the multitude of her people; for many waters are many peoples, according to John in the Apocalypse[[Apoc 17:1||]][[Apoc 17:15||]]. Or: the waters in whose defence the Ninivites trusted are like the waters of a pool, not the waters of the sea, that is, useless for resisting the Chaldeans. Therefore it is added: [[2:8|but the men flee away|Ipsi vero fugerunt]], that is, the Ninivites and Assyrians fled from the face of the Chaldeans. As they flee, others more steadfast cry: [[2:8|Stand, stand|State, state]], that is, do not flee, but fight; [[2:8|but there is none that will return back|et non est qui revertatur]], that is, none of them dared to come back. Therefore it is now said to the Chaldeans:

paras.t: Diripite argentum, diripite aurum, id est, omnia pretiosa Ninive tollite; et non est finis divitiarum ex omnibus vasis desiderabilibus, id est, infinitæ quodammodo sunt divitiæ urbis Ninive ceterarumque urbium ejus, in vasis aureis atque argenteis.
paras.en: [[2:9|Take ye the spoil of the silver, take the spoil of the gold|Diripite argentum, diripite aurum]], that is, carry off all the precious things of Ninive; [[2:9|for there is no end of the riches of all the precious furniture|et non est finis divitiarum ex omnibus vasis desiderabilibus]] [*vasa desiderabilia*, literally "desirable vessels"], that is, the riches of the city of Ninive and of her other cities, in vessels of gold and silver, are in a manner without end.

paras.t: Dissipata est Ninive, id est demolita, et scissa, et dilacerata in muris et habitaculis suis; et cor tabescens, id est, corda Ninivitarum intra se contabuerunt seu defecerunt; et dissolutio geniculorum, id est, genua eorum tremore concussa sunt: unde diminutive genicula appellantur; et defectio in cunctis renibus, id est, in visceribus eorum ac interioribus præ magnitudine pavoris fuerunt torsio atque debilitas; et facies omnium illorum, sicut nigredo ollæ, id est deformes et discoloratæ ex fame, timore, luctu, aliisque pressuris. His similia, imo et eadem specie, scribunt de Babylone Isaias et Jeremias.
paras.en: [[2:10|She is destroyed|Dissipata est]], Ninive, that is, demolished, [[2:10|and rent, and torn|et scissa, et dilacerata]] in her walls and dwellings; [[2:10|the heart melteth|et cor tabescens]], that is, the hearts of the Ninivites wasted away or failed within them; [[2:10|and the knees fail|et dissolutio geniculorum]], that is, their knees were shaken with trembling: and so they are called by the diminutive *genicula* [that is, "little knees"]; [[2:10|and all the loins lose their strength|et defectio in cunctis renibus]], that is, in their bowels and inward parts there was wrenching and weakness from the greatness of their dread; [[2:10|and the faces of them all are as the blackness of a kettle|et facies omnium illorum, sicut nigredo ollæ]], that is, disfigured and discoloured by hunger, fear, mourning and other afflictions. Things like these, and indeed of the very same kind, Isaias[[Is 13:7||]][[Is 13:8||]] and Jeremias[[Jer 50:43||]] write of Babylon.

paras.t: Ubi est habitaculum leonum? id est, ubi jam est Ninive, civitas illa eximia in qua leones, id est reges, demorati sunt? Et ubi jam pascua catulorum leonum, id est eadem civitas, vel opulentia ejus, in qua nutriti sunt filii regum illustres ac principes? ad quam expugnandam ivit leo, id est Nabuchodonosor rex : de quo loquitur Jeremias, Ascendit leo de cubili suo; ut ingrederetur illuc, id est, eam obtineret, catulus leonis, id est filius ejus, vel, ut aliqui textus habent, Cum catulis suis, id est filiis atque principibus; et non est qui exterreat, id est, nullus Assyriorum prædictum leonem potuit perterrere aut superare.
paras.en: [[2:11|Where is now the dwelling of the lions|Ubi est habitaculum leonum]]? that is, where now is Ninive, that excellent city in which lions, that is, kings, dwelt? And where now is [[2:11|the feeding place of the young lions|pascua catulorum leonum]], that is, the same city, or its wealth, in which the illustrious sons of kings and the princes were reared? [[2:11|To which|ad quam]], to storm it, [[2:11|the lion went|ivit leo]], that is, king Nabuchodonosor, of whom Jeremias speaks: [[Jer 4:7|The lion is come up out of his den|Ascendit leo de cubili suo]]; [[2:11|to enter in thither|ut ingrederetur illuc]], that is, to take possession of it, [[2:11|the young lion|catulus leonis]], that is, his son; or, as some texts have, *With his whelps*, that is, with his sons and princes; [[2:11|and there was none to make them afraid|et non est qui exterreat]], that is, none of the Assyrians could frighten or overcome the aforesaid lion.

paras.t: Leo cepit sufficienter catulis suis, id est, Nabuchodonosor satis multa prædatus est de bonis Assyriorum, deditque ea filiis suis atque principibus, et necavit leænis suis, id est, spoliatos occidit, quatenus bona eorum leænis, puta uxoribus et concubinis suis, conferret; et implevit præda speluncas suas, id est, loca thesaurorum abscondita implevit de prædis, et cubile suum implevit rapina.
paras.en: [[2:12|The lion caught enough for his whelps|Leo cepit sufficienter catulis suis]], that is, Nabuchodonosor took a great deal of booty from the goods of the Assyrians, and gave it to his sons and princes, [[2:12|and killed for his lionesses|et necavit leænis suis]], that is, he slew those he had despoiled, so as to bestow their goods on his lionesses, namely his wives and concubines; [[2:12|and he filled his holes with prey|et implevit præda speluncas suas]], that is, he filled the hidden places of his treasures with spoils, [[2:12|and his den|et cubile suum]] he filled [[2:12|with rapine|rapina]].

paras.t: Ecce ego ad te venio per visitantem vindictam, o Ninive, dicit Dominus Deus exercituum; et succendam per manum Chaldæorum usque ad summum, id est usque ad pulveres atque totaliter, quadrigas tuas, per quas alios tribulasti; et leunculos tuos, id est filios regis, seu nobiles et judices, audaces et fortes, comedet gladius Chaldæorum; et exterminabo de terra prædam tuam, id est, alios ultra non spoliabis, sed spolia quæ collegisti, tollam de terra tua, dans ea Chaldæis, ut in Babyloniam transferantur; et non audietur ultra vox nuntiorum tuorum, quos ad diversa regna mittere consuevisti, ut a gentibus tibi subditis tributa exigerent, et alias litteras comminatorias ferrent : quemadmodum nuntii Sennacherib portabant ad Ezechiam litteras blasphemiis plenas.
paras.en: [[2:13|Behold I come against thee|Ecce ego ad te venio]], by vengeance that visits thee, O Ninive, [[2:13|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus Deus exercituum]]; [[2:13|and I will burn|et succendam]], by the hand of the Chaldeans, [[2:13|even to smoke|usque ad summum]] [the text printed reads *usque ad summum*, "even to the uttermost"; the margin gives the reading *fumum*, "smoke", as in the Vulgate], that is, to dust and utterly, [[2:13|thy chariots|quadrigas tuas]], with which thou hast afflicted others; and [[2:13|thy young lions|leunculos tuos]], that is, the king's sons, or the nobles and judges, bold and strong, [[2:13|the sword shall devour|comedet gladius]], the sword of the Chaldeans; [[2:13|and I will cut off thy prey out of the land|et exterminabo de terra prædam tuam]], that is, thou shalt no more despoil others, but the spoils which thou hast gathered I will take from thy land, giving them to the Chaldeans, to be carried into Babylonia; [[2:13|and the voice of thy messengers shall be heard no more|et non audietur ultra vox nuntiorum tuorum]], whom thou wast wont to send to divers kingdoms, to exact tribute from the nations subject to thee, and at other times to carry threatening letters: as the messengers of Sennacherib carried to Ezechias letters full of blasphemies[[2 Par 32:17||]].

paras.t: Insuper de moralitate hujus capituli hoc est tenendum, quod ea quæ de Ninive scripta sunt, ad mundum referuntur, cujus (ut in præcedenti dicebatur articulo) figura fuerat Ninive.
paras.en: Further, as to the moral sense of this chapter, it is to be held that what is written of Ninive is referred to the world, of which (as was said in the preceding article) Ninive had been a figure.

paras.t: Mundo ergo nunc dicitur : Ascendit qui dispergat coram te : id est, Satan contra te consurgit, ut in oculis tuis hominibus tentando prævaleat, omnemque spiritualium auferat divitiarum possessionem; qui custodit obsidionem, id est, infatigabiliter et usque in finem vitæ præsentis observat et circumvallat te, tanquam leo rugiens circuiendo, et quem devoret exquirendo. Unde in medio laqueorum ambulamus. Ut ergo evadas ac vincas, fac quod subjungitur :
paras.en: To the world, then, it is now said: [[2:1|He is come up that shall destroy before thy face|Ascendit qui dispergat coram te]]: that is, Satan rises up against thee, to prevail over men by tempting them before thine eyes, and to take away all possession of spiritual riches; [[2:1|that shall keep the siege|qui custodit obsidionem]] [the text printed has *custodit*, "keeps"; the margin gives the reading *custodiat*, as in the Vulgate], that is, tirelessly and to the end of the present life he watches thee and hems thee in, going about [[1 Pet 5:8|as a roaring lion|tanquam leo rugiens]], and [[1 Pet 5:8|seeking whom he may devour|quem devoret exquirendo]]. Hence we walk in the midst of snares. That thou mayest escape, then, and overcome, do what is added:

paras.t: Contemplare viam, id est, Christum considera, ejusque vestigia imitare, qui ait : Ego sum via, veritas et vita. Contemplare quoque quæ sit via virtutis, via arcta, et porta angusta ducens ad vitam : de qua loquitur Jeremias, Interrogate quæ sit via bona, et ambulate in ea (et neque ad dexteram, neque ad sinistram) ; Salomon quoque, Viam sapientiæ monstrabo tibi, et currens non habebis offendiculum. Contemplare etiam viam qua tentator contra te venit, id est modos atque insidias diabolicarum tentationum : quomodo aliquando mala sub specie boni proponit, transfigurans se in angelum lucis ; nonnunquam vero evidenter mala proponit : tamen interdum hoc facit valde latenter ac fraudulenter, sicut dum viris virtuosis gloriam suggerit vanam, aut superbiæ quiddam interserit. Conforta lumbos virtute castitatis, quemadmodum ait Salvator : Sint lumbi vestri præcincti, hoc est, concupiscentiis reluctare, et carnem cum vitiis mortifica. Robora virtutem tuam valde, id est, naturalem potentiam per gratiam ora firmari, et in virtutibus satage stabiliri : imo et habitus virtuosos per actiones sanctas atque frequentes confirma, ut radicentur omnino in te, quemadmodum scriptum est in libro Josue : Confortare, et esto robustus valde. Hanc autem virtutem debemus præcipue in adversis habere, ut invicta sit patientia nostra, nec ultionem quæramus, pensantes quod Dominus ait : Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam. Unde nunc subditur :
paras.en: [[2:1|Watch the way|Contemplare viam]], that is, consider Christ and follow in his footsteps, who says: [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life|Ego sum via, veritas et vita]]. Consider also which is the way of virtue: [[Matt 7:14|strait is the way|via arcta]], and [[Matt 7:14|narrow is the gate|porta angusta]] that leads to life; of which Jeremias speaks: [[Jer 6:16|ask|Interrogate]] [[Jer 6:16|which is the good way, and walk ye in it|quæ sit via bona, et ambulate in ea]] (and turn neither to the right hand nor to the left); and Solomon too: [[Prov 4:11|I will shew thee the way of wisdom|Viam sapientiæ monstrabo tibi]], and [[Prov 4:12|when thou runnest, thou shalt not meet a stumblingblock|currens non habebis offendiculum]]. Consider also the way by which the tempter comes against thee, that is, the manners and snares of the devil's temptations: how at times he puts forward evil under the appearance of good, as he [[2 Cor 11:14|transformeth himself into an angel of light|transfigurans se in angelum lucis]]; sometimes he puts forward evil openly; yet at times he does this very secretly and deceitfully, as when he suggests vainglory to virtuous men, or slips in some touch of pride. [[2:1|Fortify thy loins|Conforta lumbos]] with the virtue of chastity, as the Saviour says: [[Luke 12:35|Let your loins be girt|Sint lumbi vestri præcincti]]; that is, struggle against concupiscences, and mortify the flesh with its vices[[Gal 5:24||]]. [[2:1|Strengthen thy power exceedingly|Robora virtutem tuam valde]] [*virtus*, both "power" and "virtue"], that is, pray that thy natural power be made firm by grace, and strive to be established in the virtues: nay, confirm also the habits of virtue by holy and frequent acts, that they may take root wholly in thee, as it is written in the book of Josue: [[Jos 1:7|Take courage|Confortare]], [[Jos 1:7|and be very valiant|et esto robustus valde]]. And this strength we must have above all in adversity, so that our patience may be unconquered, and we may not seek revenge, considering that the Lord says: [[Heb 10:30|Vengeance belongeth to me, and I will repay|Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam]][[Deut 32:35||]]. Hence it is now added:

paras.t: Quia sicut reddidit Dominus superbiam Jacob, id est, quemadmodum ultus est injuriam illatam activis in vitiorum luctamine positis, qui designantur per Jacob, qui luctator vel supplantator interpretatur, sic superbiam Israel, id est, sic ulciscetur injuriam contemplativis illatam, qui significantur per Israel, quod interpretatur vir videns Deum ; quia vastatores dissipaverunt eos, id est, mundus, caro et dæmones tentaverunt et persecuti sunt bonos, tam activos quam speculativos. Propter quod in Judith libro habetur : Omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tentationes transierunt fideles. Propagines eorum corruperunt, id est, filios eorum seu opera vitiis infecerunt, inducendo ad culpam.
paras.en: [[2:2|For the Lord hath rendered the pride of Jacob|Quia sicut reddidit Dominus superbiam Jacob]], that is, just as he avenged the wrong done to the active, who are set in the struggle against vices and are signified by Jacob, which is interpreted *wrestler* or *supplanter*, [[2:2|as the pride of Israel|sic superbiam Israel]], that is, so will he avenge the wrong done to the contemplatives, who are signified by Israel, which is interpreted *a man seeing God*; [[2:2|because the spoilers have laid them waste|quia vastatores dissipaverunt eos]], that is, the world, the flesh and the demons have tempted and persecuted the good, the active as well as the contemplative. Wherefore it is said in the book of Judith: [[Jdt 8:23|all that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful|Omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tentationes transierunt fideles]] [Denis has *tentationes*, "temptations", where the Vulgate has *tribulationes*]. They [[2:2|have marred their vine branches|Propagines eorum corruperunt]], that is, they have infected their sons, or their works, with vices, leading them into sin.

paras.t: Clypeus fortium, id est militum Christi, qui hostibus animæ efficaciter reluctantur, est ignitus fervore dilectionis. Clypeus iste, fides est caritate succensa, juxta illud ad Ephesios, In omnibus sumentes scutum fidei ; vel justitia, prout Sapiens asserit, Sumet scutum inexpugnabile æquitatem ; vel sermo divinus, secundum quod Salomon loquitur, Omnis sermo Dei ignitus, clypeus est omnibus sperantibus in se. Viri exercitus, id est, qui ad Christi exercitum pertinent, sunt in coccineis, id est, ad sanguinis sui effusionem pro Christo et fide seu æquitate parati ; vel, In coccineis, id est ferventi rubore amoris Dei et proximi. Igneæ habenæ currus, id est, vehicula quibus feruntur contra adversarios Dei, puta virtutes, sunt promptæ ac agiles, in die præparationis ejus, dum pugnam contra præfatos æmulos Christi committunt. Et agitatores ejus consopiti sunt, id est, tractatores mundi hujus, a gratia defecerunt.
paras.en: [[2:3|The shield of his mighty men|Clypeus fortium]], that is, of the soldiers of Christ, who resist the enemies of the soul with effect, [[2:3|is like fire|est ignitus]], aflame with the fervour of love. This shield is faith kindled by charity, according to that word to the Ephesians: [[Eph 6:16|In all things taking the shield of faith|In omnibus sumentes scutum fidei]]; or justice, as the Wise man asserts: [[Wis 5:20|He will take equity for an invincible shield|Sumet scutum inexpugnabile æquitatem]]; or the word of God, as Solomon says: [[Prov 30:5|Every word of God is fire tried: he is a buckler to them that hope in him|Omnis sermo Dei ignitus, clypeus est omnibus sperantibus in se]] [*ignitus*, "fiery", the word used of the shield in this verse]. [[2:3|The men of the army|Viri exercitus]], that is, those who belong to the army of Christ, [[2:3|are clad in scarlet|sunt in coccineis]], that is, ready to shed their blood for Christ and for the faith or for equity; or, *in scarlet*, that is, in the fervent red of the love of God and of neighbour. [[2:3|The reins of the chariot are flaming|Igneæ habenæ currus]], that is, the vehicles by which they are borne against the adversaries of God, namely the virtues, are ready and nimble, [[2:3|in the day of his preparation|in die præparationis ejus]], when they join battle against the aforesaid rivals of Christ. [[2:3|And the drivers are stupefied|Et agitatores ejus consopiti sunt]], that is, those who busy themselves with this world have fallen away from grace.

paras.t: In itineribus conturbati sunt, id est, in operibus suis inordinate se habent, et variis modis turbantur. Non enim est pax impiis, dicit Dominus ; et, Turbati sunt omnes insipientes corde. Denique peccatori dedit Deus afflictionem et curam superfluam, ut dicit Ecclesiastes. Quadrigæ collisæ sunt in plateis : id est, præsidia horum terrena ac vana dejecta sunt in lata hujus sæculi via, ita quod manum Judicis summi non quibunt effugere, nec debitas pœnas evadere. Adspectus eorum quasi lampades, quasi fulgura discurrentia. Hoc accipi potest in bono et in malo. Adspectus enim electorum in virtutibus perfectorum, terribilis est parti adversæ, seu dæmonibus, ut castrorum acies ordinata. Dæmones quoque horribiles sunt, præsertim imperfectis, et propter eos oportet nos esse timentes atque sollicitos. Recte quoque fulguri comparantur, quum dicat Salvator : Videbam Satanam sicut fulgur de cœlo cadentem.
paras.en: [[2:4|They are in confusion in the ways|In itineribus conturbati sunt]], that is, they behave inordinately in their works, and are troubled in various ways. For [[Is 48:22|there is no peace to the wicked, saith the Lord|Non enim est pax impiis, dicit Dominus]]; and, [[Ps 75:6|All the foolish of heart were troubled|Turbati sunt omnes insipientes corde]]. And again, [[Eccles 2:26|to the sinner he hath given vexation, and superfluous care|peccatori dedit Deus afflictionem et curam superfluam]], as Ecclesiastes says. [[2:4|The chariots jostle one against another in the streets|Quadrigæ collisæ sunt in plateis]]: that is, their earthly and vain defences are cast down on the broad way of this world, so that they will not be able to escape the hand of the supreme Judge, nor avoid the punishment due to them. [[2:4|Their looks are like torches, like lightning running to and fro|Adspectus eorum quasi lampades, quasi fulgura discurrentia]]. This can be taken in a good sense and in a bad. For the look of the elect who are perfect in the virtues is terrible to the opposing side, that is, to the demons, [[Cant 6:9|as an army set in array|ut castrorum acies ordinata]]. The demons too are dreadful, especially to the imperfect, and because of them we must be fearful and watchful. And rightly are they likened to lightning, since the Saviour says: [[Luke 10:18|I saw Satan like lightning falling from heaven|Videbam Satanam sicut fulgur de cœlo cadentem]].

paras.t: Velociter ascendent muros ejus. Per hoc designatur, quod amatores sæculi videntes se divino judicio coarctari, quærent refugium in creaturis. Et tunc præparatur eis umbraculum, id est, a vanis atque carnalibus consolatoribus datur eis spes infructuosa ac fallax, qua se putant protegere a calore indignationis divinæ : in cujus misericordia sperant sæpe inaniter, non intendentes ex toto corde postponere vitia.
paras.en: [[2:5|They shall quickly get upon the walls thereof|Velociter ascendent muros ejus]]. By this is signified that the lovers of the world, seeing themselves hemmed in by the divine judgment, will seek refuge in creatures. And then [[2:5|a covering shall be prepared|præparatur eis umbraculum]] for them, that is, by vain and carnal comforters a fruitless and deceitful hope is given them, with which they think to shield themselves from the heat of the divine indignation: in whose mercy they often hope in vain, not intending with their whole heart to put away their vices.

paras.t: Portæ fluviorum apertæ sunt, id est, conscientiæ eorum Deo patebunt, et aliis manifestabuntur, ut cognoscatur divini judicii æquitas. Templum quoque, id est ecclesia malignantium, solo tenus destruetur.
paras.en: [[2:6|The gates of the rivers are opened|Portæ fluviorum apertæ sunt]], that is, their consciences will lie open to God, and will be made manifest to others, that the equity of the divine judgment may be known. [[2:6|The temple|Templum]] also, that is, the church of the malignant, will be destroyed to the ground.

paras.t: Et miles captivus abductus est, id est, magnates sæculi a diabolo capti atque a Deo aversi sunt ; et ancillæ ejus minabantur, id est, carnales mollities, et feminæ cum quibus fornicati sunt, simul cum illis in damnationem ducentur, gementes ut columbæ : juxta illud Sapientiæ, Videntes turbabuntur terrore horribili, præ angustia spiritus gementes.
paras.en: [[2:7|And the soldier is led away captive|Et miles captivus abductus est]], that is, the great men of the world have been taken captive by the devil and turned away from God; [[2:7|and her bondwomen were led away|et ancillæ ejus minabantur]], that is, their carnal soft living, and the women with whom they have committed fornication, will be led together with them into damnation, [[2:7|mourning as doves|gementes ut columbæ]]: according to that word of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:2|These seeing it, shall be troubled with terrible fear|Videntes turbabuntur terrore horribili]], [[Wis 5:3|groaning for anguish of spirit|præ angustia spiritus gementes]].

paras.t: Et Ninive, quasi piscina aquarum aquæ ejus : id est, fluenta doctrinæ hujus mundi arctata sunt, et ad salutem inidonea, quoniam stultam fecit Deus sapientiam hujus mundi, qui (ut dictum est) per Niniven designatur ; ipsi vero, id est homines mundani, in quibus aquæ istæ abundant, fugerunt a vera sapientia Christi, a fidei simplicitate, et via justitiæ. Quæ enim stulta sunt mundi, eligit Deus, ut confundat sapientes. De quibus ait Salvator ad Patrem : Abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus. Istos invitat Ecclesia ut cessent a fuga ista : State, state ; et non est qui revertatur ad Deum per pœnitentiam, sed de vanitate in vanitatem procedunt.
paras.en: [[2:8|And as for Ninive, her waters are like a great pool|Et Ninive, quasi piscina aquarum aquæ ejus]]: that is, the streams of the teaching of this world are straitened, and unfit for salvation, since [[1 Cor 1:20|God made foolish the wisdom of this world|stultam fecit Deus sapientiam hujus mundi]], which (as has been said) is signified by Ninive; [[2:8|but the men|ipsi vero]], that is, worldly men, in whom these waters abound, [[2:8|flee away|fugerunt]] from the true wisdom of Christ, from the simplicity of faith, and from the way of justice. For [[1 Cor 1:27|the foolish things of the world hath God chosen, that he may confound the wise|Quæ enim stulta sunt mundi, eligit Deus, ut confundat sapientes]]. Of these the Saviour says to the Father: [[Matt 11:25|thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent|Abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus]]. These the Church invites to cease from this flight: [[2:8|Stand, stand|State, state]]; [[2:8|but there is none that will return back|et non est qui revertatur]] to God by penance, but they go on from vanity to vanity.

paras.t: Diripite argentum, id est nitorem sæcularis eloquentiæ, diripite aurum, id est, fulgorem mundanæ scientiæ auferte ab istis, ut discant humilitati et simplicitati insistere : quod si noluerint, auferentur eis omnia hæc tempore mortis. Et non est finis divitiarum mundi seu hominum mundanorum. De quibus Baruch ait : Ubi sunt principes gentium, et qui dominantur super bestias terræ, qui in avibus cœli ludunt, qui argentum thesaurizant et aurum, in quo confidunt homines, et non est finis acquisitionis eorum?
paras.en: [[2:9|Take ye the spoil of the silver|Diripite argentum]], that is, the polish of secular eloquence, [[2:9|take the spoil of the gold|diripite aurum]], that is, take away from these men the glitter of worldly knowledge, that they may learn to apply themselves to humility and simplicity: and if they will not, all these things will be taken from them at the time of death. [[2:9|For there is no end of the riches|Et non est finis divitiarum]] of the world, or of worldly men. Of whom Baruch says: [[Bar 3:16|Where are the princes of the nations, and they that rule over the beasts that are upon the earth|Ubi sunt principes gentium, et qui dominantur super bestias terræ]], [[Bar 3:17|That take their diversion with the birds of the air|qui in avibus cœli ludunt]], [[Bar 3:18|That hoard up silver and gold, wherein men trust, and there is no end of their getting|qui argentum thesaurizant et aurum, in quo confidunt homines, et non est finis acquisitionis eorum]]?

paras.t: Dissipata est, et scissa, et dilacerata : id est, congregatio sæcularium hominum firmitatem virtutum amisit, corde divisa est, et vitiis lacerata. Vel sensus est, quod omnis viror, gloria atque prosperitas hujus mundi cito pertransit, quemadmodum in Isaia dicitur : Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis gloria ejus quasi flos agri ; et primo libro Machabæorum : A verbis viri peccatoris ne timueritis, quia gloria ejus stercus et vermis ; hodie extollitur, et cras non invenietur, quia conversus est in terram suam, et cogitatio ejus periit. Horum est cor tabescens in malis, et dissolutio geniculorum, id est languor virtutis progressivæ de bono in melius. Contra quod Isaias et Paulus hortantur genua debilia roborari. Et defectio in cunctis renibus, ita quod passionibus appetitus sensitivi franguntur atque vincuntur. Et facies omnium sicut nigredo ollæ : id est, intellectus eorum carnalis et vitiis obscuratus est, imo turpissimus, quum nulla visibilis macula rem materialem tantum deformet, quantum mortale peccatum faciem animæ. Omnia quoque hæc corporaliter accident impiis in die judicii, secundum sensum prætactum.
paras.en: [[2:10|She is destroyed, and rent, and torn|Dissipata est, et scissa, et dilacerata]]: that is, the gathering of worldly men has lost the firmness of the virtues, is divided in heart, and torn by vices. Or the sense is that all the freshness, glory and prosperity of this world quickly passes away, as is said in Isaias: [[Is 40:6|All flesh is grass, and all the glory thereof as the flower of the field|Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis gloria ejus quasi flos agri]]; and in the first book of Machabees: [[1 Mach 2:62|fear not the words of a sinful man, for his glory is dung and worms|A verbis viri peccatoris ne timueritis, quia gloria ejus stercus et vermis]]; [[1 Mach 2:63|Today he is lifted up, and tomorrow he shall not be found, because he is returned into his earth and his thought is come to nothing|hodie extollitur, et cras non invenietur, quia conversus est in terram suam, et cogitatio ejus periit]]. In these men [[2:10|the heart melteth|cor tabescens]] in evils, [[2:10|and the knees fail|et dissolutio geniculorum]], that is, there is a faintness of the power of going forward from good to better [*virtus progressiva*, the power of walking, by which one moves forward]. Against which Isaias and Paul exhort that the weak knees be strengthened[[Is 35:3||]][[Heb 12:12||]]. [[2:10|And all the loins lose their strength|Et defectio in cunctis renibus]], in that they are broken and overcome by the passions of the sensitive appetite. [[2:10|And the faces of them all are as the blackness of a kettle|Et facies omnium sicut nigredo ollæ]]: that is, their understanding is carnal and darkened by vices, nay most foul, since no visible stain disfigures a material thing so much as mortal sin disfigures the face of the soul. All these things will also befall the wicked bodily on the day of judgment, according to the sense touched on above.

paras.t: Ubi est habitaculum leonum, et pascua catulorum leonum? Hoc nunc dici potest de quacumque civitate magnifica et regali, in qua reges, principes seu magnates morantur et deliciantur, quum fuerit demolita. Sed in fine mundi dicetur hoc generaliter de cunctis habitaculis reproborum et divitum atque nobilium. Tunc enim lætabuntur justi, videntes vindictam, et innocens subsannabit iniquos zelo justitiæ, applaudens censuræ mentis divinæ. Ad quam ivit leo, id est diabolus, ad tentandum, ut ingrederetur illuc catulus leonis, id est angelus Satanæ, ut habitaret in cordibus mundanorum. Potest quoque per catulum leonis Antichristus intelligi, cujus adventui viam præparabit diabolus, discissionem in Ecclesia procurando.
paras.en: [[2:11|Where is now the dwelling of the lions, and the feeding place of the young lions|Ubi est habitaculum leonum, et pascua catulorum leonum]]? This can now be said of any magnificent and royal city in which kings, princes or great men dwell and take their pleasure, once it has been demolished. But at the end of the world it will be said generally of all the dwellings of the reprobate, and of the rich and the noble. For then [[Ps 57:11|the just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge|lætabuntur justi, videntes vindictam]], and [[Job 22:19|the innocent shall laugh|innocens subsannabit]] the wicked to scorn with zeal for justice, applauding the sentence of the divine mind. [[2:11|To which the lion went|Ad quam ivit leo]], that is, the devil, to tempt, [[2:11|to enter in thither|ut ingrederetur illuc]], [[2:11|the young lion|catulus leonis]], that is, the angel of Satan, to dwell in the hearts of worldly men. By *the young lion* Antichrist may also be understood, for whose coming the devil will prepare the way by procuring division in the Church.

paras.t: Leo cepit sufficienter catulis suis, id est, princeps aliquis tenebrarum multos valde vinculis culpæ irretivit, qui dæmonibus sibi subjectis dantur ad puniendum, et necavit leænis suis, id est, aeriis potestatibus strangulavit animas miserorum ; et implevit præda, id est animabus a se deceptis, speluncas suas, id est foveas infernales : quæ tamen nondum perfecte impletæ sunt, præsertim quum infernus nunquam dicat, Sufficit.
paras.en: [[2:12|The lion caught enough for his whelps|Leo cepit sufficienter catulis suis]], that is, some prince of darkness has caught very many in the bonds of sin, who are handed over to the demons subject to him to be punished, [[2:12|and killed for his lionesses|et necavit leænis suis]], that is, he has strangled the souls of the wretched for the powers of the air; [[2:12|and he filled|et implevit]] [[2:12|with prey|præda]], that is, with souls deceived by him, [[2:12|his holes|speluncas suas]], that is, the pits of hell: which nevertheless are not yet perfectly filled, above all since hell[[Prov 30:16||]] [[Prov 30:15|never saith: It is enough|nunquam dicat, Sufficit]].

paras.t: Ecce ego ad te, o munde, dicit Dominus; et succendam in fine mundi, vel interim particulariter, quadrigas tuas, id est humana auxilia, in quibus inaniter es confisus ; et leunculos tuos, id est principum filios audaces, pomposos, comedet gladius tentationis seu persecutionis ac divinæ ultionis, præcipue in die judicii, quando ex ore Christi exibit gladius ex utraque parte acutus ; et exterminabo de terra prædam tuam, ita quod alios ultra non opprimes sive prædaberis. Cetera patent.
paras.en: [[2:13|Behold I come against thee|Ecce ego ad te]], O world, [[2:13|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]]; [[2:13|and I will burn|et succendam]], at the end of the world, or meanwhile in particular cases, [[2:13|thy chariots|quadrigas tuas]], that is, the human helps in which thou hast vainly trusted; and [[2:13|thy young lions|leunculos tuos]], that is, the bold and pompous sons of princes, [[2:13|the sword shall devour|comedet gladius]], the sword of temptation, or of persecution and of divine vengeance, above all on the day of judgment, when out of the mouth of Christ shall go forth [[Apoc 19:15|a sharp two-edged sword|gladius ex utraque parte acutus]]; [[2:13|and I will cut off thy prey out of the land|et exterminabo de terra prædam tuam]], so that thou shalt no more oppress or plunder others. The rest is plain.

3.title: Elucidatio capituli tertii: Væ, civitas sanguinum.
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: Woe to thee, O city of blood.

paras.t: Consequenter Ninivitarum scelera describuntur. Væ, civitas sanguinum, id est, væ temporalis vastitatis atque æternæ damnationis imminet tibi, o Ninive, quæ es urbs sanguinem fundens injuste, et operibus sanguinis plena ; universa mendacii, id est mendaciis omnino intenta; dilaceratione, id est prædarum et pauperum oppressionibus, plena. Vel dilacerationes dicuntur intestina mala mutuæ dissensionis inter cives : quod est futuræ propinquæ destructionis indicium, quum dicat Salvator, Omne regnum contra se divisum, desolabitur. Non recedet a te rapina, id est, alios spoliare non desines, quousque id poteris. Vel sensus est, quod Chaldæi non cessabunt bona ejus diripere, donec omnino demoliti fuerint eam.
paras.en: Next the crimes of the Ninivites are described. [[3:1|Woe to thee, O city of blood|Væ, civitas sanguinum]], that is, the woe of temporal devastation and of eternal damnation hangs over thee, O Ninive, who art a city that sheds blood unjustly and is full of works of blood; [[3:1|all full of lies|universa mendacii]], that is, wholly bent on lies; [[3:1|and violence|dilaceratione]] [the Latin *dilaceratio* means a tearing to pieces], that is, [[3:1|full|plena]] of plunderings and oppressions of the poor. Or the *tearings* are the inward evils of mutual dissension among the citizens: which is a sign of destruction to come soon, since the Saviour says, [[Matt 12:25|Every kingdom divided against itself shall be made desolate|Omne regnum contra se divisum, desolabitur]]. [[3:1|rapine shall not depart from thee|Non recedet a te rapina]], that is, thou wilt not cease to despoil others as long as thou canst. Or the sense is that the Chaldeans will not cease to plunder her goods until they have utterly demolished her.

paras.t: Vox flagelli, id est sonitus percussionis qua alios afflixisti, et vox impetus rotæ, et equi frementis, et quadrigæ ferventis, id est sonitus impetuosæ motionis rotarum et equorum ad bellum frementium, et quadrigarum per quas alios devastasti, et equitis ascendentis, id est hominum ascendentium equos, vel consurgentium contra alios, et micantis gladii, et fulgurantis hastæ, id est sonitus politorum gladiorum splendentiumque hastarum, et multitudinis interfectæ, id est cadaverum a Ninivitis occisorum : qui et multos filiorum Israel jugulaverunt in Ninive diebus Tobiæ ; et gravis ruinæ, qua alios oppressisti ; nec est finis, id est numerus faciliter computabilis, cadaverum, quæ exstinxerunt et interfecerunt Assyrii, quorum principales fuerant Ninivitæ, qui quos per potentiam superare non poterant, fraudibus dejecerunt. Omnia itaque mala hæc fuerunt in Ninivitis.
paras.en: [[3:2|The noise of the whip|Vox flagelli]], that is, the sound of the blows with which thou didst afflict others, [[3:2|and the noise of the rattling of the wheels, and of the neighing horse; and of the running chariot|et vox impetus rotæ, et equi frementis, et quadrigæ ferventis]], that is, the sound of the violent onrush of the wheels and of the horses snorting for battle, and of the chariots with which thou didst lay others waste, [[3:2|and of the horsemen coming up|et equitis ascendentis]], that is, of men mounting horses, or rising up against others, [[3:3|And of the shining sword, and of the glittering spear|et micantis gladii, et fulgurantis hastæ]], that is, the sound of polished swords and gleaming spears, [[3:3|and of a multitude slain|et multitudinis interfectæ]], that is, of the corpses of those killed by the Ninivites: who also slaughtered many of the children of Israel in Ninive in the days of Tobias[[Tob 1:21||]]; [[3:3|and of a grievous destruction|et gravis ruinæ]], with which thou didst crush others; [[3:3|and there is no end|nec est finis]], that is, no number that can easily be counted, [[3:3|of carcasses|cadaverum]] which the Assyrians destroyed and slew, of whom the Ninivites were the chief; and those whom they could not overcome by power they brought down by frauds. All these evils, then, were in the Ninivites.

paras.t: Idcirco Et corruent in corporibus suis, id est, etiam ipsi a Chaldæis occidentur, cadetque unus super alium, propter multitudinem fornicationum spiritualium Ninive, id est idololatriæ, quoniam teste Hieronymo, omnium gentium a se victarum idolis Ninive ministravit ; carnalium quoque fornicationum, quia in omnibus serviebant libidini ; meretricis speciosæ et gratæ, id est Ninive, quæ suis amatoribus placuit, et omnibus mundi ornamentis fulgebat, et habentis maleficia, id est opera magorum, ariolorum, maleficorum, quos intra se continebat; quæ vendidit gentes in fornicationibus suis : id est, per avaritias suas, et ut voluptatibus satisfacerent, vendebant gentes sibi subditas in servos atque ancillas ; vel, ut alii dicunt, posuerunt decoras puellas et juvenes forma egregios, quos ceperant, pro pretio in prostibulis ; et familias vendiderunt in maleficiis suis : de quibus jam dictum est.
paras.en: Therefore [[3:3|they shall fall down on their dead bodies|Et corruent in corporibus suis]], that is, they too shall be slain by the Chaldeans, and one shall fall upon another, [[3:4|Because of the multitude of the fornications|propter multitudinem fornicationum]] of Ninive: spiritual fornications, that is, idolatry, since, as Jerome witnesses, Ninive served the idols of all the nations she had conquered; and carnal fornications too, for in all things they were slaves to lust; [[3:4|of the harlot that was beautiful and agreeable|meretricis speciosæ et gratæ]], that is, of Ninive, who pleased her lovers and shone with all the ornaments of the world, [[3:4|and that made use of witchcraft|et habentis maleficia]], that is, the works of magicians, soothsayers and sorcerers, whom she kept within her; [[3:4|that sold nations through her fornications|quæ vendidit gentes in fornicationibus suis]]: that is, through their avarice, and to satisfy their pleasures, they sold the nations subject to them as bondmen and bondwomen; or, as others say, they set comely girls and youths of outstanding beauty, whom they had captured, in brothels for hire; [[3:4|and families|et familias]] they sold [[3:4|through her witchcrafts|in maleficiis suis]]: of which we have spoken already.

paras.t: Deinde tantorum vitiorum annectitur pœna : Ecce ego ad te, o Ninive, dicit Dominus exercituum ; et revelabo pudenda tua in facie tua, id est, faciam te a Chaldæis nudari, sicque verecundiora tua patebunt, et ostendam gentibus tibi adversantibus nuditatem tuam, et regnis ignominiam tuam, id est confusionem et derisionem. Et projiciam super te abominationes tuas, id est, debitas punitiones propter detestabilia opera tua, et ea quæ aliis intulisti, jam patieris ; et contumeliis afficiam te, id est, Chaldæis te tradam, qui te ignominiose tractabunt ; et ponam te in exemplum, id est, tam dire te corrigam, quod alii terrebuntur, et punitionem tuam pro exemplo suscipient, ne et ipsi patiantur similia.
paras.en: Then the punishment of such great vices is added: [[3:5|Behold I come against thee|Ecce ego ad te]], O Ninive, [[3:5|saith the Lord of hosts: and I will discover thy shame to thy face|dicit Dominus exercituum ; et revelabo pudenda tua in facie tua]], that is, I will have thee stripped by the Chaldeans, and so thy more shameful parts will lie open, and I will shew to the nations that are hostile to thee [[3:5|thy nakedness|nuditatem tuam]], [[3:5|and thy shame to kingdoms|et regnis ignominiam tuam]], that is, thy confusion and their mockery. [[3:6|And I will cast abominations upon thee|Et projiciam super te abominationes]], thine own, that is, the punishments due for thy detestable works, and what thou didst inflict on others thou shalt now suffer; [[3:6|and will disgrace thee|et contumeliis afficiam te]], that is, I will deliver thee to the Chaldeans, who will treat thee shamefully; [[3:6|and will make an example of thee|et ponam te in exemplum]], that is, I will chastise thee so terribly that others will be terrified, and will take thy punishment as an example, lest they too suffer the like.

paras.t: Et erit : Omnis qui viderit te in tanta miseria positam, resiliet a te, id est, fugiet, nec tibi auxiliari præsumet, et dicet : Vastata est Ninive. Quasi dicat : Quum talis ac tanta capta sit civitas, quis non formidet ? Quis commovebit super te caput ex compassione? id est, quis condolebit tibi? quasi dicat, Pauci aut nemo. Caput, secundum Hieronymum, non habetur in Hebræo ; sed Hieronymus addidit propter evidentiam faciendam in sensu. Unde quæram consolatorem tibi ? id est, tanta erit desolatio tua, quod non poterit tibi consolatio impertiri; nec digna es consolatore, quæ in tua potestate nullius miserebaris; nec socium tuo luctui præparasti, quæ noluisti consortem habere regnandi.
paras.en: [[3:7|And it shall come to pass that every one that shall see thee|Et erit : Omnis qui viderit te]], set in such misery, [[3:7|shall flee from thee|resiliet a te]], that is, shall run away, and shall not venture to help thee, [[3:7|and shall say: Ninive is laid waste|et dicet : Vastata est Ninive]]. As if to say: when a city so great and so mighty has been taken, who will not be afraid? [[3:7|who shall bemoan thee?|Quis commovebit super te caput]] [literally, 'who shall move the head over thee?'] out of compassion? that is, who will grieve with thee? as if to say, few or none. *The head*, according to Jerome, is not in the Hebrew; but Jerome added it to make the sense plain. [[3:7|whence shall I seek a comforter for thee?|Unde quæram consolatorem tibi ?]] that is, so great will thy desolation be that no comfort can be given thee; nor art thou worthy of a comforter, who in thy power hadst pity on no one; nor hast thou got thyself a companion for thy mourning, who wouldst have no partner in thy reigning.

paras.t: Denique quod Ninive fuerit destruenda, ostenditur per locum a majori. Numquid, o Ninive, melior, id est numero civium major sive potentior, es ab, id est quam, Alexandria populorum, id est civitas Ægypti sic dicta, plurimum populosa ? Quæ olim vocabatur No ; sed quum a Chaldæis destructam diu postmodum ædificasset Alexander Magnus, nominavit eam Alexandriam. Unde Nahum propheta non ait, Alexandria ; sed Hieronymus in commento suo ostendit, quod loquitur de urbe hac, et sic in textu positum est, Ab Alexandria: quod aliqui ab Hieronymo asserunt factum ; verumtamen in suo textu ita non ponit, ut intuentibus constat. Quæ habitat in fluminibus, id est inter flumina. Sita est enim inter Nilum ex una parte, et mare ex altera parte, et lacum Mareoticum. Aquæ in circuitu ejus : cujus divitiæ sunt mare, id est ea quæ per mare deferuntur ad eam ; aquæ muri ejus, id est fortitudo ipsius tanquam muri : ita quod Alexandria tam muris quam aquis protegitur.
paras.en: Lastly, that Ninive was to be destroyed is shown by an argument from the greater [that is, what befell a greater city will much more befall a lesser one]. [[3:8|Art thou|Numquid]], O Ninive, [[3:8|better|melior]], that is, greater in number of citizens, or more powerful, [[3:8|than|es ab]] [the Latin has *es ab*, literally 'art thou … from', which Denis explains as *quam*, 'than'] [[3:8|the populous Alexandria|Alexandria populorum]], that is, the city of Egypt so called, exceedingly populous? It was once called No; but when Alexander the Great rebuilt it, long after it had been destroyed by the Chaldeans, he named it Alexandria. So the prophet Nahum does not say *Alexandria*; but Jerome in his commentary shows that he is speaking of this city, and so *Ab Alexandria* was put in the text: which some assert was done by Jerome; yet in his own text he does not put it so, as is plain to those who look. [[3:8|that dwelleth among the rivers|Quæ habitat in fluminibus]], that is, between rivers. For it lies between the Nile on one side, and the sea on the other, and Lake Mareotis. [[3:8|waters are round about it: the sea is its riches|Aquæ in circuitu ejus : cujus divitiæ sunt mare]], that is, what is brought to it by sea; [[3:8|the waters are its walls|aquæ muri ejus]], that is, its strength, as of walls: so that Alexandria is protected as much by waters as by walls.

paras.t: Æthiopia fortitudo ejus, id est, Æthiopes fuerunt ei confœderati et auxiliarii, et Ægyptus, id est, ceteræ urbes Ægypti fuerunt ei præsidio, quoniam ipsa fuit illarum metropolis. Et non est finis divitiarum et fortitudinis hujus urbis : per quod designatur eximia abundantia, non absoluta infinitas. Africa et Libyes fuerunt in auxilio tuo, o Alexandria. Sed et ipsa in transmigratione ducta est in captivitatem, id est, non obstantibus omnibus jam prædictis, Alexandria a Chaldæis capietur, et populus ejus transferetur seu occidetur. Nabuchodonosor enim rex Babylonis cepit hanc urbem, quando vastavit Ægyptum. Parvuli ejus elisi sunt in capite omnium viarum. Chaldæi namque ex crudelitate nec parvulis pepercerunt, sed in capitibus platearum eliserunt eosdem; et super inclytos ejus, id est nobiles Alexandriæ, miserunt Chaldæi sortem, qui quos captivos acciperent ; et omnes optimates ejus confixi sunt in compedibus, id est graviter vincti.
paras.en: [[3:9|Ethiopia|Æthiopia]] [[3:9|were the strength thereof|fortitudo ejus]], that is, the Ethiopians were her confederates and auxiliaries, [[3:9|and Egypt|et Ægyptus]], that is, the other cities of Egypt were her defence, since she was their capital. [[3:9|and there is no end|Et non est finis]] of the riches and strength of this city: by which an outstanding abundance is signified, not infinity in the strict sense. [[3:9|Africa and the Libyans were thy helpers|Africa et Libyes fuerunt in auxilio tuo]], O Alexandria. [[3:10|Yet she also was removed and carried into captivity|Sed et ipsa in transmigratione ducta est in captivitatem]], that is, notwithstanding all that has been said, Alexandria will be taken by the Chaldeans, and her people carried away or slain. For Nabuchodonosor, king of Babylon, took this city when he laid Egypt waste. [[3:10|her young children were dashed in pieces at the top of every street|Parvuli ejus elisi sunt in capite omnium viarum]]. For the Chaldeans in their cruelty did not spare even the little ones, but dashed them at the heads of the streets; and [[3:10|upon her nobles|super inclytos ejus]], that is, the nobles of Alexandria, the Chaldeans [[3:10|cast|miserunt]] [[3:10|lots|sortem]], to settle who should take whom as captives; [[3:10|and all her great men were bound in fetters|et omnes optimates ejus confixi sunt in compedibus]], that is, heavily chained.

paras.t: Et tu ergo, o Ninive, inebriaberis, id est, calice similium pœnarum ad plenum potaberis, et eris despecta, quæ alios despexisti, ut impleatur in te illud Isaiæ : Væ qui spernis, nonne et ipse sperneris ? Quum fatigatus desieris contemnere, contemneris. Chaldæi etenim sine reverentia tractarunt Alexandriæ cives. Et tu quæres auxilium ab inimico : id est, in tantam necessitatem devenies, ut a gentibus te odientibus quæras contra Chaldæos subsidium. Aliqui enim tempore angustiæ quærunt facere amicitiam cum his cum quibus paulo ante discordiam habuerunt, ut tunc succursum impendant. Sed non facile inveniuntur tempore adversitatis præsidia quæ non erant requisita tempore prosperitatis aut merita.
paras.en: [[3:11|Therefore thou also|Et tu ergo]], O Ninive, [[3:11|shalt be made drunk|inebriaberis]], that is, thou shalt be given to drink to the full of the cup of like punishments, [[3:11|and shalt be despised|et eris despecta]], who didst despise others, that there may be fulfilled in thee that saying of Isaias: [[Is 33:1|Woe to thee|Væ]] [[Is 33:1|that despisest, shalt not thyself also be despised?|qui spernis, nonne et ipse sperneris ?]] [[Is 33:1|when being wearied thou shalt cease to despise, thou shalt be despised|Quum fatigatus desieris contemnere, contemneris]]. For the Chaldeans treated the citizens of Alexandria [so the print; one would expect Ninive] without reverence. [[3:11|and thou shalt seek help from the enemies|Et tu quæres auxilium ab inimico]]: that is, thou shalt come into such need that thou wilt seek aid against the Chaldeans from the nations that hate thee. For some, in a time of distress, seek to make friends with those with whom they were at odds a little before, so that these may then bring them succour. But in the time of adversity defences are not easily found that were not sought, or deserved, in the time of prosperity.

paras.t: Omnes munitiones tuæ, id est muri ac pugnatores tui, ac cetera tua auxilia, erunt sicut ficus cum grossis suis, id est, primi temporis ficubus comparabuntur ; si concussæ fuerint, cadent in os comedentis : id est, quemadmodum tales ficus seu grossi, facili motu moventur et dejiciuntur, ut manducentur ; sic tuæ munitiones a Chaldæis impugnatæ, dejicientur ac devorabuntur. Ecce populus tuus, o Ninive, mulieres, id est effeminatus, formidolosus, et impotens, Chaldæis non valens resistere, in medio tui. Inimicis tuis adapertione pandentur portæ terræ tuæ, id est, portæ tuæ et urbium terræ tuæ, scilicet Assyriorum, aperientur Chaldæis, et eis pandentur ad introeundum ; devorabit ignis vectes tuos, id est, ferreas clausuras consumet : per quod insinuatur vehemens fore incendium Ninive.
paras.en: [[3:12|All thy strong holds|Omnes munitiones tuæ]], that is, thy walls and thy fighting men and the rest of thy defences, will be [[3:12|like fig trees with their green figs|sicut ficus cum grossis suis]], that is, they will be likened to the figs of the early season; [[3:12|if they be shaken, they shall fall into the mouth of the eater|si concussæ fuerint, cadent in os comedentis]]: that is, as such figs, or green figs, are moved and shaken down with a slight movement, to be eaten, so thy strongholds, assailed by the Chaldeans, will be thrown down and devoured. [[3:13|Behold thy people|Ecce populus tuus]], O Ninive, [[3:13|are women|mulieres]], that is, effeminate, fearful and powerless, unable to resist the Chaldeans, [[3:13|in the midst of thee|in medio tui]]. [[3:13|the gates of thy land shall be set wide open to thy enemies|Inimicis tuis adapertione pandentur portæ terræ tuæ]], that is, thy gates and those of the cities of thy land, namely of the Assyrians, will be opened to the Chaldeans and thrown wide for them to enter; [[3:13|the fire shall devour thy bars|devorabit ignis vectes tuos]], that is, it will consume the iron fastenings: by which it is suggested that the burning of Ninive will be fierce.

paras.t: Aquam propter obsidionem hauri tibi, id est, de potu provide tibi, o Ninive, propter vallationem hostilem tibi instantem. Hoc et sequentia aliqui ironice proferunt, ad innuendum quod nulla provisio Ninivitis prodesset. Exstrue munitiones tuas, id est turres muri. Intra in lutum, et calca, id est, lateres confice, et propugnacula effice, et subigens tene laterem, id est, lateres serva ad ædificandum ea quibus protegaris. Ibi comedet te ignis, id est, aliqui tuorum incendentur. Vel per ignem quælibet dira afflictio designatur. Peribis gladio Chaldæorum, ita quod quidam tuorum gladio occidentur ; devorabit te gladius, ut bruchus devorat fructus. Congregare ergo ut bruchus, multiplicare ut locusta : id est, populus tuus congregetur in unum, et in quamcumque multitudinem poterit, colligatur et augeatur, ut se ad repugnandum disponat ; nil tamen proficiet, quoniam a Chaldæis superabuntur. Bruchus autem et locusta solent in magna multitudine in unum confluere.
paras.en: [[3:14|Draw thee water for the siege|Aquam propter obsidionem hauri tibi]], that is, provide thyself with drink, O Ninive, because of the hostile investment that threatens thee. Some take this and what follows as spoken ironically, to hint that no provision would profit the Ninivites. [[3:14|build up thy bulwarks|Exstrue munitiones tuas]], that is, the towers of the wall. [[3:14|go into the clay, and tread|Intra in lutum, et calca]], that is, make bricks and build ramparts, and [[3:14|work it and make brick|subigens tene laterem]] [literally, 'working it, hold the brick'], that is, keep bricks for building the works by which thou mayest be protected. [[3:15|There shall the fire devour thee|Ibi comedet te ignis]], that is, some of thy people will be burnt. Or by fire any dire affliction is meant. [[3:15|thou shalt perish by the sword|Peribis gladio]] of the Chaldeans, so that some of thy people will be slain by the sword; [[3:15|it shall devour thee|devorabit te]], the sword shall, [[3:15|like the bruchus|ut bruchus]] devouring the fruits [the *bruchus* is a kind of locust; the Douay-Rheims keeps the Latin word]. [[3:15|assemble together like the bruchus, make thyself many like the locust|Congregare ergo ut bruchus, multiplicare ut locusta]]: that is, let thy people be gathered into one, and be collected and increased to whatever multitude it can, so as to make ready to resist; yet it will avail nothing, since they will be overcome by the Chaldeans. Now the bruchus and the locust are wont to flock together in great multitudes.

paras.t: Plures fecisti negotiationes tuas, quam stellæ sint cœli, id est, infatigabiliter congregasti divitias per diversas atque innumerabiles mercaturas : quæ hyperbolice, id est per excessum, dicuntur excedere numerum siderum, ad insinuandum multitudinem mercationis tuæ et cupiditatis insatiandæ. Bruchus expansus est et avolavit, id est, natis sibi alis, extendit se ad avolandum. Custodes tui quasi locustæ, id est invalidi ad præservandum te a malo captivitatis : sicque expandes te per modum bruchi ad fugiendum a facie Chaldæorum ; et parvuli tui quasi locustæ locustarum, id est, in maxima multitudine sunt, sicut locustarum genimina, quæ dicuntur ἀττέλεβοι, quæ locustæ considunt, id est, pariter sedent, in sepibus in die, id est tempore, frigoris : torpent enim in frigore, et in sepibus colligunt se, ut a frigore abscondantur, quantum possibile est, quia a frigore faciliter moriuntur. Sol ortus est, et avolaverunt, id est, calore solis recepto, quasi reviviscunt et avolant, et non est cognitus locus earum, ubi fuerint. Non enim manent indicia pristinæ consessionis, sed aer intra se clauditur. Per hoc significatur, quod Ninivitæ ceterique Assyrii, timore, ut frigore quodam, torperent ac latitarent, deinde in captivitatem volarent aut fugerent.
paras.en: [[3:16|Thou hast multiplied thy merchandises above the stars of heaven|Plures fecisti negotiationes tuas, quam stellæ sint cœli]], that is, thou hast tirelessly heaped up riches by divers and countless tradings: which are said hyperbolically, that is, by way of excess, to exceed the number of the stars, to suggest the great amount of thy trading and of thy insatiable greed. [[3:16|the bruchus hath spread himself and flown away|Bruchus expansus est et avolavit]], that is, wings having grown on it, it has stretched itself out to fly away. [[3:17|Thy guards are like the locusts|Custodes tui quasi locustæ]], that is, powerless to keep thee from the evil of captivity: and so thou wilt spread thyself out like the bruchus to flee from the face of the Chaldeans; [[3:17|and thy little ones like the locusts of locusts|et parvuli tui quasi locustæ locustarum]], that is, they are in very great multitude, like the brood of locusts, which are called ἀττέλεβοι [*attelaboi*, the Greek name for young, wingless locusts], which locusts [[3:17|swarm|considunt]], that is, settle together, [[3:17|on the hedges in the day|in sepibus in die]], that is, in the time, [[3:17|of cold|frigoris]]: for they grow numb in the cold, and gather themselves in the hedges to hide from the cold as far as they can, since they easily die of cold. [[3:17|the sun arose, and they flew away|Sol ortus est, et avolaverunt]], that is, having taken in the heat of the sun, they as it were revive and fly off, [[3:17|and their place was not known where they were|et non est cognitus locus earum, ubi fuerint]]. For no traces of their former settling together remain, but the air closes up on itself. By this it is signified that the Ninivites and the other Assyrians, numbed by fear as by a kind of cold, would lie torpid and hidden, and then would fly away into captivity, or flee.

paras.t: Dormitaverunt pastores tui, o rex Assur : id est, duces et consules tui, o rex Assyriorum, qui regnasti in Ninive, dormierunt somno mortis a Chaldæis occisi, et cessaverunt tibi dare consilium, atque ignavi effecti sunt ; sepelientur principes tui. Minus dicit, et majus significat, id est, crudeliter occidentur, et irreverenter sepelientur, quemadmodum de rege Juda Joakim loquitur Jeremias : Quia sepultura asini sepelietur. Latitavit, o Ninive, populus tuus in montibus, timore Chaldæorum se abscondens in locis difficilis accessus atque sublimis situs, ut procul viderent si hostes venirent, et non est qui congreget, id est, adunet eos, ut facto exercitu rebellent Chaldæis.
paras.en: [[3:18|Thy shepherds have slumbered, O king of Assyria|Dormitaverunt pastores tui, o rex Assur]]: that is, thy captains and counsellors, O king of the Assyrians, who didst reign in Ninive, have slept the sleep of death, slain by the Chaldeans, and have ceased to give thee counsel, and have become sluggish; [[3:18|thy princes shall be buried|sepelientur principes tui]]. He says less and means more [the figure called litotes or meiosis], that is, they will be cruelly slain and buried without honour, as Jeremias says of Joakim, king of Juda: For [[Jer 22:19|He shall be buried with the burial of an ass|sepultura asini sepelietur]]. [[3:18|thy people|populus tuus]], O Ninive, [[3:18|are hid|Latitavit]] [[3:18|in the mountains|in montibus]], hiding themselves for fear of the Chaldeans in places hard of access and lofty of site, so as to see from afar whether the enemy were coming, [[3:18|and there is none to gather them|et non est qui congreget]], that is, to unite them, so that they might form an army and rebel against the Chaldeans.

paras.t: Non est obscura contritio tua, id est, destructio tua aperta est, et omnibus nota, pessima est plaga tua, id est pœnalissima et insanabilis. Omnes qui audierunt auditionem tuam, id est formam destructionis tuæ, compresserunt manum super te, non ex compassione, ut dictum est, et quia subjungitur : quia super quem non transiit malitia tua semper? id est, jugiter a tua fundatione alios crudeliter afflixisti, in tantum ut pene nulla natio tuæ pravitatis vexationem evaserit. Compresserunt igitur manum super te, complosis manibus tuæ dejectioni congratulando, insultando et applaudendo, paratiores tuam calamitatem gravare, quam alleviare. Potuit tamen accidere, quod multi, audita Ninive demolitione, doluerunt, non illi compatiendo, sed sibimetipsis timendo, desperantes se posse Chaldæorum evadere manum, a quibus tam famosissimam urbem audierunt vastatam.
paras.en: [[3:19|Thy destruction is not hidden|Non est obscura contritio tua]], that is, thy destruction is open and known to all, [[3:19|thy wound is grievous|pessima est plaga tua]], that is, most painful and incurable. [[3:19|all that have heard the fame of thee|Omnes qui audierunt auditionem tuam]], that is, the manner of thy destruction, [[3:19|have clapped their hands over thee|compresserunt manum super te]] [literally, 'have pressed the hand together over thee'], not out of compassion, as has been said, and because there follows: [[3:19|for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?|quia super quem non transiit malitia tua semper?]] that is, from thy foundation thou hast unceasingly and cruelly afflicted others, so much that hardly any nation has escaped the harassment of thy wickedness. So they have clapped their hands over thee, striking their hands together in rejoicing at thy overthrow, mocking and applauding, readier to make thy calamity heavier than to lighten it. Yet it may have happened that many, on hearing of the demolition of Ninive, grieved, not out of compassion for her, but out of fear for themselves, despairing of being able to escape the hand of the Chaldeans, by whom they heard that so very famous a city had been laid waste.

paras.t: Denique juxta spiritualem intelligentiam, ut dictum est, per Ninive designatur hic mundus in maligno positus, cujus amicitia inimica Deo est, in quo quidquid est, aut est concupiscentia carnis, aut concupiscentia oculorum, aut superbia vitæ. Unde quæ in hoc capitulo ad litteram dicta sunt de culpa et pœna Ninive, ad totius mundi culpam et pœnam tropologice referuntur. Quod quomodo fieri queat, non prosequor propter prolixitatem vitandam, et quoniam ex superioribus pro magna parte patescit ; sed aliqua breviter dicam, tangendo magis quam explicando.
paras.en: Lastly, according to the spiritual understanding, as has been said, Ninive here signifies the world that is [[1 John 5:19|seated in wickedness|in maligno positus]], [[Jas 4:4|the friendship|cujus amicitia]] of which [[Jas 4:4|is the enemy of God|inimica Deo est]], in which whatever there is, is either [[1 John 2:16|the concupiscence of the flesh|concupiscentia carnis]], or [[1 John 2:16|the concupiscence of the eyes|concupiscentia oculorum]], or [[1 John 2:16|the pride of life|superbia vitæ]]. Hence what has been said in this chapter, according to the letter, of the guilt and punishment of Ninive is referred tropologically [that is, in the moral sense] to the guilt and punishment of the whole world. How this can be done I do not pursue, to avoid prolixity, and because it is plain for the most part from what has gone before; but I will say a few things briefly, touching on them rather than explaining them.

paras.t: Væ, civitas sanguinum. Hæc est ecclesia malignantium, congregatio reproborum, generatio mala, vitiis plena, mendaciis dedita, per schismata et hæreses aliaque facinora dilacerata : a qua non recedit rapina, quum ipsi se invicem spolient, fallant, depauperent ; et dæmones de cordibus illorum spirituales divitias rapiunt, imo et naturales perfectiones animæ tollunt, ita quod lumine rationis non utens, passionibus ducitur, bestialiterque versatur.
paras.en: [[3:1|Woe to thee, O city of blood|Væ, civitas sanguinum]]. This is the church of the malignant, the congregation of the reprobate, an evil generation, full of vices, given over to lies, torn to pieces by schisms and heresies and other crimes: from which [[3:1|rapine|rapina]] does not depart, since they despoil, deceive and impoverish one another; and the demons snatch spiritual riches from their hearts, nay, they take away even the natural perfections of the soul, so that, not using the light of reason, it is led by the passions and lives like a beast.

paras.t: Porro, in hac civitate, non Dei, sed Babylonis, est Væ flagelli, id est sonitus tribulationum, quibus justos affligunt [maligni], vel se mutuo tribulant. Inter superbos enim semper sunt jurgia, et impii quasi mare fervens, quod quiescere non potest. Et vox impetus rotæ, id est inordinatæ evaginationis : quia non stabiliuntur in Deo, sed undique evagantur, juxta illud Psalmi, In circuitu impii ambulant ; et, Deus meus, pone illos ut rotam ; et equi frementis, id est tyrannorum ; et quadrigæ ferventis, id est mali vehiculi quod quatuor principalibus animæ passionibus trahitur, nisi per rationis censuram frenentur, videlicet delectatione et tristitia, spe et timore ; et micantis gladii, et fulgurantis hastæ, id est, apparentis prosperitatis ac deceptoriæ delectationis, quibus velut hasta ac ense animæ impiorum necantur ac fodiuntur. Creaturæ etenim factæ sunt in muscipulam et laqueum pedibus insipientium. Est quoque in ea vox multitudinis interfectæ, id est peccatorum, qui vitam gratiæ amiserunt, et in mortem peccati per tentationem illapsi sunt, et gravis ruinæ a spiritualibus ad carnalia, a virtutibus ad vitia, ab imperio Christi ad regnum diaboli : et quanto est anima præstantior corpore, tanto gravior est ejus ruina quam corporis. Nec est finis cadaverum, id est corporum vitiosorum : quæ dicuntur cadavera, quoniam animæ a quibus informantur, sunt mortuæ coram Deo, nec ab eis aliquid spiritualis virtuosæque vitæ participant. Propter quod scriptum est : Corpus mortuum est propter peccatum ; et, Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos.
paras.en: Further, in this city, which is not God's but Babylon's, there is [[3:2|the noise of the whip|Væ flagelli]] [the print reads *Væ flagelli*, 'woe of the whip', apparently for *Vox flagelli*], that is, the sound of the tribulations with which the wicked afflict the just, or trouble one another. For [[Prov 13:10|Among the proud there are always contentions|Inter superbos enim semper sunt jurgia]], and [[Is 57:20|the wicked are like the raging sea, which cannot rest|impii quasi mare fervens, quod quiescere non potest]]. [[3:2|and the noise of the rattling of the wheels|Et vox impetus rotæ]], that is, of disordered wandering abroad [*evagatio*, the straying of the mind outward, away from God, among created things]: for they are not made steadfast in God, but wander about on every side, according to that of the Psalm, [[Ps 11:9|The wicked walk round about|In circuitu impii ambulant]]; and, [[Ps 82:14|O my God, make them like a wheel|Deus meus, pone illos ut rotam]]; [[3:2|and of the neighing horse|et equi frementis]], that is, of tyrants; [[3:2|and of the running chariot|et quadrigæ ferventis]], that is, of the evil vehicle that is drawn by the four principal passions of the soul, unless they are reined in by the censure of reason: namely delight and sorrow, hope and fear; [[3:3|And of the shining sword, and of the glittering spear|et micantis gladii, et fulgurantis hastæ]], that is, of seeming prosperity and deceitful delight, by which, as by spear and sword, the souls of the wicked are slain and pierced. For creatures [[Wis 14:11|are turned|factæ sunt]] into a trap and [[Wis 14:11|a snare to the feet of the unwise|laqueum pedibus insipientium]]. There is also in it the noise [[3:3|of a multitude slain|multitudinis interfectæ]], that is, of sinners, who have lost the life of grace and have slipped through temptation into the death of sin, [[3:3|and of a grievous destruction|et gravis ruinæ]] [*ruina* is both 'destruction' and 'fall'] from spiritual things to carnal, from virtues to vices, from the empire of Christ to the kingdom of the devil: and the more excellent the soul is than the body, the more grievous is its fall than the body's. [[3:3|and there is no end of carcasses|Nec est finis cadaverum]], that is, of vicious bodies: which are called carcasses because the souls by which they are informed [that is, given their form and life, the soul being the form of the body] are dead before God, and they share in nothing of the spiritual and virtuous life. Wherefore it is written: [[Rom 8:10|the body indeed is dead, because of sin|Corpus mortuum est propter peccatum]]; and, [[Matt 8:22|let the dead bury their dead|Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos]].

paras.t: Corruent in corporibus suis, id est vitiis carnis : si enim secundum carnem vixerimus, moriemur ; propter multitudinem fornicationum meretricis speciosæ et gratæ, id est earum cum quibus nunc fornicantur. Qui enim fornicatur, in corpus suum peccat ; et qui conjungitur meretrici, unum cum ea corpus efficitur. Unde et Salomon : Favus, inquit, distillans labia meretricis ; novissima autem illius, amara quasi absynthium. Ipsa enim est fovea profunda, et rete diaboli.
paras.en: [[3:3|they shall fall down on their dead bodies|Corruent in corporibus suis]], that is, through the vices of the flesh: for [[Rom 8:13|if you live according to the flesh, you shall die|si enim secundum carnem vixerimus, moriemur]] [Denis has it in the first person: 'if we live …, we shall die']; [[3:4|Because of the multitude of the fornications of the harlot that was beautiful and agreeable|propter multitudinem fornicationum meretricis speciosæ et gratæ]], that is, of those with whom they now commit fornication. For [[1 Cor 6:18|he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body|Qui enim fornicatur, in corpus suum peccat]]; and [[1 Cor 6:16|he who is joined to a harlot is made one body|qui conjungitur meretrici, unum cum ea corpus efficitur]]. Wherefore Solomon too: [[Prov 5:3|a honeycomb dropping|Favus]], he says, [[Prov 5:3|the lips of a harlot|distillans labia meretricis]]; [[Prov 5:4|But her end is bitter as wormwood|novissima autem illius, amara quasi absynthium]]. For she is [[Prov 23:27|a deep ditch|fovea profunda]], and the net of the devil.

paras.t: Ecce ego ad te puniendum, dicit Dominus exercituum ; et revelabo pudenda tua, id est inhonesta ac turpia opera, in facie tua : id est, tam stricte et evidenter ulciscar tua peccata, quod per experientiam scies quid feceris. Et ostendam gentibus nuditatem tuam, id est spiritualem paupertatem. Istud fit interdum in sæculo isto, sed maxime fiet in futuro judicio, quando Judex cœlestis cunctis ostendet scelera reproborum.
paras.en: [[3:5|Behold I come against thee|Ecce ego ad te]] to punish thee, [[3:5|saith the Lord of hosts: and I will discover thy shame|dicit Dominus exercituum ; et revelabo pudenda tua]], that is, thy dishonourable and shameful works, [[3:5|to thy face|in facie tua]]: that is, I will avenge thy sins so strictly and so plainly that thou shalt know by experience what thou hast done. [[3:5|and will shew thy nakedness to the nations|Et ostendam gentibus nuditatem tuam]], that is, thy spiritual poverty. This happens at times in this world, but it will happen above all at the judgment to come, when the heavenly Judge will shew to all the crimes of the reprobate.

paras.t: Omnis qui viderit te, resiliet a te. Tunc enim justi omnino separabuntur loco, voto, ac præmio ab injustis, quibus nunc corporaliter admiscentur. Nunc quoque multi applaudunt miscenturque malis, quorum quum viderint plagam, se subtrahunt, atque terrentur. Quis commovebit super te caput ? Unde quæram consolatorem tibi ? In die quippe judicii non erit tempus compassionis et consolationis, sed lætabitur justus videns vindictam.
paras.en: [[3:7|every one that shall see thee, shall flee from thee|Omnis qui viderit te, resiliet a te]]. For then the just will be wholly separated from the unjust, in place, in desire and in reward, though now they are mingled with them in body. Now too many applaud the wicked and mix with them, and when they see their scourge, they withdraw and are terrified. [[3:7|who shall bemoan thee?|Quis commovebit super te caput ?]] [[3:7|whence shall I seek a comforter for thee?|Unde quæram consolatorem tibi ?]] For in the day of judgment there will be no time for compassion and consolation, but [[Ps 57:11|The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge|lætabitur justus videns vindictam]].

paras.t: Numquid melior es ab Alexandria populorum ? Quum aliqua particularis congregatio prava et sæcularis, stulte secura est, nec timet judicium Dei, sed suis in viribus fidens, præsumit et jactat se non perituram, proponamus ei in exemplum aliam congregationem perversam, numero et potestate majorem, a Deo propter peccata sua plagatam, atque dicamus : Numquid melior es, etc. ? id est, sicut illa, ita et tu prorsus peribis.
paras.en: [[3:8|Art thou better than the populous Alexandria|Numquid melior es ab Alexandria populorum]]? When some particular congregation, wicked and worldly, is foolishly secure and does not fear the judgment of God, but trusting in its own strength presumes and boasts that it will not perish, let us set before it as an example another perverse congregation, greater in number and power, smitten by God for its sins, and let us say: [[3:8|Art thou better|Numquid melior es]], etc.? that is, as she did, so shalt thou too utterly perish.

paras.t: Ecce, o munde et immunde, populus tuus est sicut mulieres, id est carnalis, mollis, vitiis delectationibusque succumbens ; et effeminati dominantur tibi. Inimicis tuis pandentur portæ terræ tuæ : id est, sensus corporis tui incustoditi sunt, ita quod dæmones ingrediuntur per eos, et mors per fenestras ingreditur. Dum enim sensus per rationem non gubernantur, innumerabilibus vicibus hauriunt mortem ; et toties dæmonibus aperiuntur, quoties ad culpam inducunt. Ideo sanctus precatur Psalmista : Averte oculos meos ne videant vanitatem ; et alius, Sepi aures tuas spinis, et noli audire linguam nequam. Devorabit ignis vectes tuos : id est, ossa corporis ardor libidinis vorat, et ad æternam flammam perducit.
paras.en: [[3:13|Behold|Ecce]], O world, thou unclean one [a play on *munde*, 'O world', and *immunde*, 'O unclean'], [[3:13|thy people|populus tuus]] are like [[3:13|women|mulieres]], that is, carnal, soft, giving way to vices and pleasures; and [[Is 3:4|the effeminate shall rule over|effeminati dominantur]] thee. [[3:13|the gates of thy land shall be set wide open to thy enemies|Inimicis tuis pandentur portæ terræ tuæ]]: that is, the senses of thy body are unguarded, so that demons enter through them, and [[Jer 9:21|death is come up through our windows|mors per fenestras ingreditur]]. For while the senses are not governed by reason, they drink in death countless times; and they are opened to the demons as often as they lead into sin. Therefore the holy Psalmist prays: [[Ps 118:37|Turn away my eyes that they may not behold vanity|Averte oculos meos ne videant vanitatem]]; and another says, [[Ecclus 28:28|Hedge in thy ears with thorns, hear not a wicked tongue|Sepi aures tuas spinis, et noli audire linguam nequam]]. [[3:13|the fire shall devour thy bars|Devorabit ignis vectes tuos]]: that is, the heat of lust devours the bones of the body, and brings it to the eternal flame.

paras.t: Deinde mundo consulitur : Aquam sapientiæ salutaris et rorem gratiæ, propter obsidionem, qua ab invisibilibus vallatus es hostibus, hauri tibi devotis precibus de fontibus Salvatoris, de ore prædicatoris, de sacris Scripturis, de fonte Sapientiæ increatæ. Exstrue munitiones tuas, id est, virtutes robora, et spiritualia arma assume ; intra in lutum, id est, corpus tuum adspice et guberna, et calca illud, ut obediat rationi ; tene laterem, id est firmitatem virtutum, et petram quæ est Christus. Et nisi hæc feceris, comedet te ignis, peribisque gladio tentationis.
paras.en: Then the world is counselled: [[3:14|Draw thee|hauri tibi]] [[3:14|water|Aquam]] of saving wisdom and the dew of grace, [[3:14|for the siege|propter obsidionem]] with which thou art beset by invisible enemies, by devout prayers, [[Is 12:3|out of the saviour's fountains|de fontibus Salvatoris]], from the mouth of the preacher, from the holy Scriptures, from the fountain of uncreated Wisdom. [[3:14|build up thy bulwarks|Exstrue munitiones tuas]], that is, strengthen the virtues, and take up spiritual arms; [[3:14|go into the clay|intra in lutum]], that is, look to thy body and govern it, [[3:14|and tread|et calca]] it, that it may obey reason; [[3:14|make brick|tene laterem]] [literally, 'hold the brick'], that is, the firmness of the virtues, and the rock which is Christ[[1 Cor 10:4||]]. And unless thou do these things, then [[3:15|shall the fire devour thee|comedet te ignis]], and [[3:15|thou shalt perish by the sword|peribisque gladio]] of temptation.
