paras.t: Custodes tui, id est principes et prælati, quasi locustæ, id est inefficaces et bestiales, te non protegentes, sed simul secum ad infernum trahentes. Tales enim merentur iniqui habere præsidentes ab eo qui regnare facit hypocritam propter peccata populi, qui dat regem in furore suo et principes in indignatione sua. Parvuli tui, id est inferiores, quasi locustæ locustarum, quæ considunt in sepibus in die frigoris. Sic isti tempore adversitatis et tribulationis, paulisper retrahuntur et cessant a malis, domique resident. Sol ortus est, et avolaverunt, id est, die prosperitatis radiante, et timore malorum sublato, discurrunt, vagantur, transgrediuntur ut ante.
paras.en: [[3:17|Thy guards|Custodes tui]], that is, princes and prelates, [[3:17|are like the locusts|quasi locustæ]], that is, ineffectual and brutish, not protecting thee, but dragging thee down with themselves to hell. For the wicked deserve to have such rulers from him [[Job 34:30|Who maketh a man that is a hypocrite to reign for the sins of the people|qui regnare facit hypocritam propter peccata populi]], who gives a king in his wrath and princes in his indignation[[Osee 13:11||]]. [[3:17|thy little ones|Parvuli tui]], that is, the lesser folk, [[3:17|like the locusts of locusts which swarm on the hedges in the day of cold|quasi locustæ locustarum, quæ considunt in sepibus in die frigoris]]. So these, in a time of adversity and tribulation, draw back for a little and cease from evil, and stay at home. [[3:17|the sun arose, and they flew away|Sol ortus est, et avolaverunt]], that is, when the day of prosperity shines and the fear of evils is taken away, they run about, roam and transgress as before.

paras.t: Dormitaverunt, scilicet somno torporis et negligentiæ, pastores tui, id est vicarii, o rex Assur, id est, magne prælate, qui alios habes tibi subjectos pastores velut vicarios, et tibi in vitiis similes sunt, sicque oves dispereunt; sepelientur principes tui in inferno cum divite epulone; latitavit populus tuus in montibus, id est, in superbiis se abscondit a gratia Dei, et in superioribus suis stulte confisus est. Non est qui congreget eos in ovile Christi. Messis quidem multa, sed operarii pauci.
paras.en: [[3:18|have slumbered|Dormitaverunt]], namely with the sleep of torpor and negligence, [[3:18|thy shepherds|pastores tui]], that is, thy vicars, [[3:18|O king of Assyria|o rex Assur]], that is, O great prelate, who hast other pastors under thee as thy vicars, and they are like thee in vices, and so the sheep perish; [[3:18|thy princes shall be buried|sepelientur principes tui]] in hell with the rich glutton[[Luke 16:22||]]; [[3:18|thy people are hid in the mountains|latitavit populus tuus in montibus]], that is, in its pride it hides itself from the grace of God, and foolishly trusts in its superiors. [[3:18|there is none to gather them|Non est qui congreget eos]] into the fold of Christ. [[Matt 9:37|The harvest indeed is great, but the labourers are few|Messis quidem multa, sed operarii pauci]].

paras.t: Non est obscura contritio tua, pessima est plaga tua. Peccata enim mundanam conversationem habentium, qui peccata sua quasi Sodoma prædicant, sunt aperta, et damnatio horum est æterna. In præsenti quoque conteruntur, omne esse gratiæ amittendo: et in hoc pessima plaga cæduntur, quod non castigantur a Deo in vita præsenti, sed in adinventionibus suis dimittuntur, atque futuris suppliciis reservantur. Omnes qui audierunt auditionem tuam, id est damnationis tuæ sententiam, Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum, compresserunt manum super te, divinæ justitiæ applaudendo, tuamque damnationem approbando. Istud erit in die judicii, quando electi judicabunt cum Christo. Quia super quem electorum hominum non transiit malitia tua semper? Nempe a principio mundi reprobi afflixerunt electos; et Abel esse renuit, quem Cain malitia non exercet. Per hunc modum purgantur electi: quo facto, reprobi projiciuntur in ignem gehennæ, quemadmodum filio castigato, jactatur virga in flammam. Non ergo propter injurias ad impatientiam concitemur, sed in omnibus summi Judicis benignissimæ dispensationi gratias referamus, qui est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus in sæcula. Amen.
paras.en: [[3:19|Thy destruction is not hidden, thy wound is grievous|Non est obscura contritio tua, pessima est plaga tua]]. For the sins of those who live a worldly life, who [[Is 3:9|have proclaimed abroad their sin as Sodom|peccata sua quasi Sodoma prædicant]], are open, and their damnation is eternal. In the present too they are crushed [*conteruntur*, the verb of *contritio*, 'destruction'], losing all the being of grace; and they are struck with the worst of wounds in this, that they are not chastised by God in the present life, but are let go in their own inventions[[Ps 80:13||]], and are kept for torments to come. [[3:19|all that have heard the fame of thee|Omnes qui audierunt auditionem tuam]], that is, the sentence of thy damnation, [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]], [[3:19|have clapped their hands over thee|compresserunt manum super te]], applauding the divine justice and approving thy damnation. This will be on the day of judgment, when the elect will judge with Christ. [[3:19|for upon whom|Quia super quem]] of the elect [[3:19|hath not thy wickedness passed continually?|non transiit malitia tua semper?]] Indeed, from the beginning of the world the reprobate have afflicted the elect; and he refuses to be Abel whom the malice of Cain does not exercise [a saying of St Gregory the Great]. In this way the elect are purged: and when this is done, the reprobate are cast into the fire of hell, as, when the son has been chastised, the rod is thrown into the flame. Let us not, then, be stirred to impatience by injuries, but in all things give thanks to the most kind dispensation of the supreme Judge, [[Rom 9:5|who is over all things, God|qui est super omnia Deus]] most high, [[Rom 9:5|blessed for ever. Amen|et benedictus in sæcula. Amen]].
